title: Mouthpieces and reeds
summary: He experiments with mouthpieces, and over the years used Van Doren, Vibrator, wartime plastic and now Rico Royal number three reeds.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yeah, in Paris. Yeah, I found that to be true. And then mouthpieces, you're always experimenting with mouthpieces and you hear something new and so you keep your ear out for something new and you try it and if it isn't what you been usin'...you don't like it as well as what you been usin'...then you don't use it. And the same thing with reeds.
Have you changed mouthpieces a lot over the years?
Well, not that often. You have to play a mouthpiece for so many years, then

you decide you want to make a change because you hear something else. And so you go out and you search again until you find what you're looking for, so that with this new sound that you hear, you know. As you grow older and mature you hear new things, of course true musicians hear sounds twenty-four hours, you know, you hear sounds all the time and you hear things. And the partiucular thing that you're looking for, you can't get it, then you try another mouthpiece, you see.
What kind of a mouthpiece do you have now?

I have an Yeah. In reeds, you know, through the years Van Doren had the best reed, then we tried Vibrator, then there was a time when things went bad, during the war, we was usin' plastic reeds. And then I finally ended up with Rico Royal, because they seem to hold up and last longer. Yeah.
What number reed are you using now?
Number three. Yeah. That Rico Royal is a very strong reed, it holds up. Yeah. It's got a nice sound to it.
